pathway.title: FAIR ISAAC CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The scoring franchise earns very high margins and turns almost all of them into cash. Derived EBITDA was USD 1,252.44 million over twelve months, 52.32% of revenue, and free cash flow was USD 960.88 million, 76.72% of EBITDA. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and capital spending only 1.48% of revenue, so a revenue loss falls to profit but reinvestment takes little cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

Leverage is the weakest dimension and policy, not operations, set it. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x at the 2025 year-end and net leverage to 4.26x from 3.11x, because total debt rose USD 2,526.70 million while derived EBITDA rose USD 312.64 million. Cash repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million were 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million in the nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-11

Interest will take more of the cash flow than the latest cover shows. Cover on interest actually paid was 7.60x, but the coupons and floating rates stated at 2026-06-30 imply about USD 316.51 million a year against USD 164.87 million paid over twelve months, so cover on current rates is 3.96x. USD 2,210.00 million of the debt floats, and the filings disclose no interest rate hedge. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07

Concentration and price dependence are the main business risk. Scores produced 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, and management attributes the Scores increase to a higher mortgage score unit price, with higher volume also contributing in the nine months, so earnings are exposed to a pricing or policy decision the company does not control. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-04

Software is not yet an offset. Segment margin was 28% for nine months against 31% a year earlier and segment operating income fell 8%, while recurring revenue rose 10% only because platform products grew 62% against a 17% fall in non-platform products with net retention of 82%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

Liquidity is adequate for twelve months but thinner than a year ago, and the maturity wall is in fiscal 2028. Cash of USD 248.44 million plus USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, gives USD 538.44 million against USD 859.14 million at the 2025 year-end and USD 300.00 million of term loan installments due within twelve months, while USD 1,987.50 million falls due in fiscal 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Governance does not offset the leverage. No sponsor or controlling holder is established to support equity, the board approved three successively larger repurchase programmes between June 2025 and June 2026, and Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk medium, moving toward high if borrowing-funded repurchases continue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36

In a Scores downturn the covenant, not cash, is the first break point. Reversing the nine-month Scores gain would cut derived EBITDA to USD 888.68 million and lift derived gross leverage to 6.28x against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x, whereas USD 400.83 million of cash after interest, tax and capital spending would still cover the USD 300.00 million of installments. The covenant's own earnings definition is not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

cells.text: Two segments. Scores sells credit scores to businesses and to consumers, including the FICO Score. Software sells analytic and decisioning software, fraud, originations and customer-management solutions and related professional services. Management describes the company as a global analytics software leader.

Usage-based royalties, mostly paid by consumer reporting agencies when a score is generated; revenue is recognised when usage occurs. The company has limited visibility on these sales until royalty reports arrive at the end of each billing period.

Multi-year subscriptions with payments based on usage, often with contracted minimums, sold as software-as-a-service or on-premises. SaaS was 62% and on-premises 38% of subscription software revenue in the nine months to 2026-06-30.
Scores 66% (USD 1,238.404 million); Software 34% (USD 639.420 million). A year earlier: Scores 58% (USD 857.023 million); Software 42% (USD 618.095 million).
Scores 59% (USD 1,168.575 million); Software 41% (USD 822.294 million). Fiscal 2023: Scores 51%, Software 49%.
Scores segment operating income was 90% of segment revenue in the nine months (91% in the third quarter, from 88%). Software was 28% in the nine months (26% in the third quarter, from 32%).

Experian, TransUnion and Equifax together generated 63% of third-quarter revenue and 60% of nine-month revenue, and each was above 10% of revenue. Together they were 51% of fiscal 2025 revenue, 45% of fiscal 2024 and 41% of fiscal 2023.
Financial services was 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the Americas 87%. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 the Americas were 90%, Europe, Middle East and Africa 7% and Asia Pacific 3%.

Annual recurring revenue was USD 815.8 million at 2026-06-30, up 10% from a year earlier, of which platform products were 51% (USD 412.8 million) and non-platform 49% (USD 403.0 million). Remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, about half expected within 14 months.

Management states that its offerings compete favourably and that many competitors are larger than the company. VantageScore, a joint venture established by the three consumer reporting agencies, sells a competing credit score.

Use of the FICO Score for mortgages sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is subject to ongoing validation by those enterprises and the Federal Housing Finance Agency. In July 2025 the agency director announced that originators may choose the credit score they submit. The company warns that legislative or regulatory limits on score fees could constrain its ability to raise mortgage score prices.
Nine months to 2026-06-30, as a share of revenue: cost of revenues 14%, research and development 9%, selling, general and administrative 24%, operating income 53%.

Capital expenditures were USD 27.845 million against operating cash flow of USD 777.880 million. Free cash flow, as the company defines it, was USD 750.035 million against net income of USD 660.003 million.
3,811 employees in 28 countries at 2025-09-30 and 3,876 at 2026-06-30; 40% were based in India at the year-end.

runs.text: Strength: Scores profitability and cash conversion. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and 91% in the third quarter, derived EBITDA margin was 52.32% over twelve months and capital spending was 1.48% of revenue, so free cash flow of USD 960.88 million covers interest and scheduled amortisation several times and could delever the company quickly if repurchases stopped. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

Strength: a staggered, mostly fixed-rate unsecured maturity profile with proven market access. The notes mature in 2028, 2033 and 2034, the revolver in 2030, USD 2.5 billion of notes was placed between May 2025 and March 2026, and the disclosed fair value of the notes was 98.04% of face value, so refinancing pressure before fiscal 2028 is limited. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-10

Strength: Software recurring revenue is shifting to a platform with high retention. Platform recurring revenue grew 62% to USD 412.8 million with net retention of 148%, and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, which adds contracted visibility to a segment that is otherwise a small part of profit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25

Weakness: borrowing-funded repurchases. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x in nine months, cash repurchases were 4.06x free cash flow, and the covenant ceiling reported after the June 2026 amendment that added the term loan is 4.5x against 3.5x before, so the board has shown a willingness to use leverage capacity for shareholders. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-09

Weakness: dependence on mortgage score price and three distributors. Scores supplied 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, the three agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue and also own a competing score, and growth leans on a unit price that regulation or competition can cap, so a single decision can reduce earnings faster than debt can be repaid. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-04

Weakness: higher interest cost and a covenant that tightens. Interest at current rates is about USD 316.51 million a year against USD 164.87 million paid, cutting cover to 3.96x, and the maximum leverage ratio falls from 4.5x to 3.5x by 2027-12-31 on a definition that is not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03

cells.text: Fair Isaac Corporation; common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as FICO.
Delaware corporation; headquarters in Bozeman, Montana.
Ends 30 September; the latest filing covers the quarter ended 2026-06-30.
Founded in 1956; 3,811 employees in 28 countries at 2025-09-30.
The chief executive officer has held the role since January 2012 and is a director. The chief financial officer has held the role since May 2023, after serving as interim from January 2023.

Deloitte & Touche LLP, auditor since 2004; opinion on the 2025 statements dated 2025-11-07. Internal control over financial reporting was effective at 2025-09-30 and disclosure controls were effective at 2026-06-30.
21,597,635 shares outstanding at 2026-07-17 and 67,259,148 held as treasury stock; 23,709,047 outstanding at 2025-10-23.
208 holders of record at 2025-10-23; market value held by non-affiliates USD 36,060,682,209 at 2025-03-31.
No cash dividend declared or paid since May 2017, and none planned.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In fiscal 2026 the company took two large financing steps. On 2026-03-20 it issued USD 1.0 billion of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds to make a payment against the revolving line and to repay in full, before its May 2026 maturity, the USD 400.0 million 5.25% notes. On 2026-06-05 it borrowed a USD 1.5 billion unsecured term loan maturing 2028-05-15 under an amended credit agreement and paid USD 1.5 billion the same day to Wells Fargo Securities under an accelerated share repurchase, receiving an initial 1,055,103 shares worth about USD 1.2 billion and prepaying USD 300.0 million for shares to be delivered when the agreement settles, expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_fico-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-03-31_fico-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-03-31_fico-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13

In fiscal 2025 the company issued USD 1.5 billion of 6.00% senior notes due 2033 on 2025-05-13, used the proceeds to repay its USD 300 million and USD 450 million term loans, and amended the credit agreement to lift the revolving line from USD 600 million to USD 1.0 billion with its maturity extended to 2030-05-13. Total debt at carrying value was USD 3,055.69 million at 2025-09-30 and USD 5,582.39 million at 2026-06-30, and the revolving line was drawn USD 710.0 million at the later date. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

No acquisition appears in the cash flow statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025 or for the nine months of fiscal 2026. The only disposal was the sale of certain assets of the Siron compliance business in fiscal 2023, with a gain of USD 1.9 million, and the only restructuring was the elimination of 226 positions in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 at a cost of USD 10.9 million. The credit agreement permits borrowings for acquisitions and share repurchases, and the leverage covenant allows a step up to 4.0x after certain permitted acquisitions, so acquisition capacity exists but no acquisition appetite is evidenced. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: FAIR ISAAC CORP (issuer id fico), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: set out the business model, ownership and control, financing and repurchase transactions, and the governance and shareholder behaviour that matter to creditors. The analysis rests on the seven supplied filings and releases dated to 2026-07-29 and on the earlier Source readiness analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earlier analysis supplied to this module is listed below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fair Isaac is a high-margin scoring franchise that depends on three distributors, and its board has chosen to fund very large share repurchases with new borrowing, so financial policy is the main risk for creditors, ahead of business risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scores produced 66% of nine-month revenue at a 90% segment margin, but its growth leaned on a higher mortgage score unit price, and three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue. Total debt rose USD 2,526.70 million in nine months as repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million reached 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million, and no sponsor or controlling holder is established to support equity. Governance and financial-policy risk is medium, moving toward high if borrowing-funded repurchases continue as the leverage covenant ceiling, raised from 3.5x to 4.5x by the June 2026 amendment, steps back to 4.0x on 2026-12-31 and 3.5x on 2027-12-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scores is the credit, and it is performing: it produced 66% of nine-month revenue at a 90% segment margin and 95% of the nine-month revenue increase, so earnings quality is high but rests on one product line. Operating cash flow was USD 777.88 million for nine months and capital spending was only 1.48% of revenue, so cash conversion is not the constraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration among distributors is rising and is, in our view, the largest business risk. Experian, TransUnion and Equifax together paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, up from 51% in fiscal 2025 and 41% in fiscal 2023, and they established VantageScore, a joint venture that sells a competing score. These distributors can ask to change the terms on which they offer the FICO Score, and the company says it has limited visibility until their royalty reports arrive, so a change in one relationship would reach the highest-margin revenue first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth in Scores leans on price, which can reverse. The company attributes the third-quarter business-to-business increase to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, its risk factors warn that limits on score fees could constrain further price increases, and the Federal Housing Finance Agency director announced in July 2025 that mortgage originators may choose the credit score they submit to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. A price or policy reversal would fall almost directly to profit because the segment's costs are small, which is our interpretation of its 91% third-quarter margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Software diversifies the business only slowly. Third-quarter software revenue rose 2%, and annual recurring revenue grew 10% to USD 815.8 million because platform products grew 62% while non-platform recurring revenue fell 17% with net retention of 82%. Segment margin fell to 26% from 32% as point-in-time licence sales declined and hosting costs rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the binding risk. Between June 2025 and June 2026 the board approved three successive repurchase programmes, each larger than the last, and nine-month repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million were 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million, so lenders and noteholders funded the gap. The USD 1.5 billion accelerated repurchase was paid on the day the USD 1.5 billion term loan was drawn, and total liabilities of USD 6,134.51 million are now 3.01x total assets of USD 2,037.37 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is only partly evidenced, and no sponsor or controlling holder is established, so there is no identified party to inject equity or cure a covenant breach. Board composition, committees, ownership and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, which leaves the board's alignment with creditors to be judged from its recorded actions, and those actions include the borrowing-funded repurchases described above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A surviving antitrust claim is a live but unquantified risk. The Sherman Act Section 2 claim and accompanying state law claims against the company continue through discovery after the court dismissed all other claims on 2024-11-24, and the filings state no material exposure for matters with a reasonable possibility of loss and give no estimate. An adverse outcome could reach the pricing and distribution practices behind Scores growth, which is an analyst interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate on terms but thin on risk. The quarterly reports state each debt instrument, the leverage covenant steps and covenant compliance, but the annual risk factors contain no stand-alone risk factor on the company's own indebtedness, and the third-quarter report says risk factors had no material changes although total debt had risen by USD 2,526.70 million since the year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–56; calculation CALC-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and market access. Free cash flow was USD 750.04 million in nine months, the Scores margin reached 91% in the third quarter, capital spending is light, and the company placed USD 1.5 billion of senior notes in May 2025 and USD 1.0 billion in March 2026 while the disclosed fair value of its senior notes was 98.04% of face value on 2026-06-30. The revolving line runs to 2030-05-13, covenant compliance is reported, no cash dividend has been paid since May 2017, and the filings record no priming, uptier or other action against existing lenders. Repurchase programmes are open-ended authorisations, not commitments, so the board can slow them at any time; only the accelerated repurchase is contractually fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Risk would fall if the board commits repurchases to free cash flow, states a leverage target, or the proxy statement shows a stable holder base and independent oversight of financial policy. It would rise if repurchases again exceed free cash flow after the covenant ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31, if the board starts a further programme funded by borrowing, if a consumer reporting agency or the federal housing regulator changes how the FICO Score is priced or used in mortgages, or if the antitrust claim produces a remedy that touches score pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement is not available, so shareholder concentration, board independence, committee oversight and related-party dealings are not established. This limits the conclusion that no controlling holder exists and could change the governance rating if a large holder or a related-party arrangement appears.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and note indentures are not available, so restricted-payment capacity, guarantor structure and the covenant's definition of earnings are not established. The conclusion that financial policy rather than legal capacity drives the risk rests on observed behaviour and could change if the documents cap repurchases or add guarantees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The terms of the distribution agreements with the three consumer reporting agencies (price schedules, term, renewal and termination rights) are not disclosed, so the durability of price-led Scores growth cannot be measured and confidence in the revenue durability view is reduced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest evidence is dated 2026-06-30, so settlement of the accelerated share repurchase and any repurchases or borrowing since then are not known. The conclusion on borrowing-funded repurchases could be out of date by the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The content of the March 2026 charter amendment is not stated in the supplied filings, so the assessment of control and takeover defences may omit a change made that month.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In fiscal 2026 the company took two large financing steps. On 2026-03-20 it issued USD 1.0 billion of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds to make a payment against the revolving line and to repay in full, before its May 2026 maturity, the USD 400.0 million 5.25% notes. On 2026-06-05 it borrowed a USD 1.5 billion unsecured term loan maturing 2028-05-15 under an amended credit agreement and paid USD 1.5 billion the same day to Wells Fargo Securities under an accelerated share repurchase, receiving an initial 1,055,103 shares worth about USD 1.2 billion and prepaying USD 300.0 million for shares to be delivered when the agreement settles, expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In fiscal 2025 the company issued USD 1.5 billion of 6.00% senior notes due 2033 on 2025-05-13, used the proceeds to repay its USD 300 million and USD 450 million term loans, and amended the credit agreement to lift the revolving line from USD 600 million to USD 1.0 billion with its maturity extended to 2030-05-13. Total debt at carrying value was USD 3,055.69 million at 2025-09-30 and USD 5,582.39 million at 2026-06-30, and the revolving line was drawn USD 710.0 million at the later date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition appears in the cash flow statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025 or for the nine months of fiscal 2026. The only disposal was the sale of certain assets of the Siron compliance business in fiscal 2023, with a gain of USD 1.9 million, and the only restructuring was the elimination of 226 positions in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 at a cost of USD 10.9 million. The credit agreement permits borrowings for acquisitions and share repurchases, and the leverage covenant allows a step up to 4.0x after certain permitted acquisitions, so acquisition capacity exists but no acquisition appetite is evidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: FAIR ISAAC CORP (issuer id fico), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: assess the issuer's fundamental credit profile, its strongest support and primary downside path, and the monitoring signals that matter to creditors. The analysis rests on the seven supplied filings and releases dated to 2026-07-29 and on the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earlier analyses supplied to this module are listed below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fair Isaac pairs a highly profitable, cash-generative scoring franchise with derived gross leverage that rose to 4.46x in nine months of borrowing-funded repurchases, so creditors depend on mortgage score pricing holding and on the board slowing repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow was USD 960.88 million over twelve months against cash interest paid of USD 164.87 million, but interest at the rates now in place is about USD 316.51 million a year, which would take cover from 7.60x to 3.96x. If the nine-month rise in Scores earnings reversed, derived leverage would reach 6.28x while cash after interest, tax and capital spending would still cover the USD 300.00 million of term loan installments due within twelve months, so a covenant test would come under pressure before liquidity. Fundamental credit quality is adequate: strong on cash conversion, weak on financial policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scoring franchise earns very high margins and turns almost all of them into cash. Derived EBITDA was USD 1,252.44 million over twelve months, 52.32% of revenue, and free cash flow was USD 960.88 million, 76.72% of EBITDA. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and capital spending only 1.48% of revenue, so a revenue loss falls to profit but reinvestment takes little cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the weakest dimension and policy, not operations, set it. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x at the 2025 year-end and net leverage to 4.26x from 3.11x, because total debt rose USD 2,526.70 million while derived EBITDA rose USD 312.64 million. Cash repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million were 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million in the nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest will take more of the cash flow than the latest cover shows. Cover on interest actually paid was 7.60x, but the coupons and floating rates stated at 2026-06-30 imply about USD 316.51 million a year against USD 164.87 million paid over twelve months, so cover on current rates is 3.96x. USD 2,210.00 million of the debt floats, and the filings disclose no interest rate hedge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration and price dependence are the main business risk. Scores produced 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, and management attributes the Scores increase to a higher mortgage score unit price, with higher volume also contributing in the nine months, so earnings are exposed to a pricing or policy decision the company does not control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Software is not yet an offset. Segment margin was 28% for nine months against 31% a year earlier and segment operating income fell 8%, while recurring revenue rose 10% only because platform products grew 62% against a 17% fall in non-platform products with net retention of 82%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for twelve months but thinner than a year ago, and the maturity wall is in fiscal 2028. Cash of USD 248.44 million plus USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, gives USD 538.44 million against USD 859.14 million at the 2025 year-end and USD 300.00 million of term loan installments due within twelve months, while USD 1,987.50 million falls due in fiscal 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance does not offset the leverage. No sponsor or controlling holder is established to support equity, the board approved three successively larger repurchase programmes between June 2025 and June 2026, and Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk medium, moving toward high if borrowing-funded repurchases continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In a Scores downturn the covenant, not cash, is the first break point. Reversing the nine-month Scores gain would cut derived EBITDA to USD 888.68 million and lift derived gross leverage to 6.28x against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x, whereas USD 400.83 million of cash after interest, tax and capital spending would still cover the USD 300.00 million of installments. The covenant's own earnings definition is not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the leverage is a choice. Free cash flow of USD 960.88 million over twelve months, applied entirely to debt, would cut derived gross leverage from 4.46x to 3.69x, the board can slow repurchases at will, and the company reports covenant compliance, placed USD 1.5 billion of senior notes in May 2025 and USD 1.0 billion in March 2026, and has senior notes whose disclosed fair value was 98.04% of face value at 2026-06-30. The first scheduled principal payments are small and the largest maturity is in fiscal 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the board stated a leverage target or limited repurchases to free cash flow, if the executed credit agreement showed covenant headroom on its own definition, or if the platform migration lifted Software margin toward its fiscal 2025 level of 30%. It would worsen if repurchases again exceeded free cash flow after the ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31, if the housing regulator or a consumer reporting agency changed how the FICO Score is priced or used in mortgages, if floating rates rose, or if Scores revenue fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization because the issuer reports none, and the covenant's own earnings definition is not available. Every leverage, cover and downside ratio here is therefore a derived measure, and the conclusion that a covenant test comes under pressure before liquidity could change if the definition adds back more cost than share-based compensation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The run-rate interest of USD 316.51 million uses coupons and the floating rates stated at 2026-06-30 and leaves out fees and issuance cost amortisation, so the 3.96x cover could be higher or lower as floating rates and margins move with leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario reverses the nine-month Scores increase mechanically and is not a forecast. The split of that increase between price and volume is not disclosed, so the likelihood and the size of a price-led reversal cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, debt quote or peer data is supplied, so the comparison of the business profile with other leveraged-credit issuers is qualitative and the view on refinancing capacity rests on issuance history and the disclosed fair value of the notes alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management guidance covers fiscal 2026 only, so the outlook beyond the next twelve to twenty-four months is not established and the medium-term assessment is limited to the direction of identified drivers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: Scores profitability and cash conversion. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and 91% in the third quarter, derived EBITDA margin was 52.32% over twelve months and capital spending was 1.48% of revenue, so free cash flow of USD 960.88 million covers interest and scheduled amortisation several times and could delever the company quickly if repurchases stopped.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: a staggered, mostly fixed-rate unsecured maturity profile with proven market access. The notes mature in 2028, 2033 and 2034, the revolver in 2030, USD 2.5 billion of notes was placed between May 2025 and March 2026, and the disclosed fair value of the notes was 98.04% of face value, so refinancing pressure before fiscal 2028 is limited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: Software recurring revenue is shifting to a platform with high retention. Platform recurring revenue grew 62% to USD 412.8 million with net retention of 148%, and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, which adds contracted visibility to a segment that is otherwise a small part of profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: borrowing-funded repurchases. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x in nine months, cash repurchases were 4.06x free cash flow, and the covenant ceiling reported after the June 2026 amendment that added the term loan is 4.5x against 3.5x before, so the board has shown a willingness to use leverage capacity for shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: dependence on mortgage score price and three distributors. Scores supplied 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, the three agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue and also own a competing score, and growth leans on a unit price that regulation or competition can cap, so a single decision can reduce earnings faster than debt can be repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: higher interest cost and a covenant that tightens. Interest at current rates is about USD 316.51 million a year against USD 164.87 million paid, cutting cover to 3.96x, and the maximum leverage ratio falls from 4.5x to 3.5x by 2027-12-31 on a definition that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fair Isaac is a US analytics software company whose profit comes mainly from Scores, a usage-based royalty on credit scores generated through consumer reporting agencies, with Software as the smaller and slower segment. This supports cash-flow visibility in activity terms but not in price terms: royalties arrive after each billing period and depend on mortgage and credit card volumes, so debt service capacity rests on activity the company does not control. Financial services supplied 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and revenue was USD 2,393.58 million over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to lean on. The supplied documents identify no controlling holder, the proxy statement with board and ownership detail was not supplied, and the board approved three successively larger repurchase programmes between June 2025 and June 2026. Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk medium, moving toward high. The group is one registrant with unnamed consolidated subsidiaries and no stated guarantors, so the priority of the unsecured debt within the group is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in Software and usage-based in Scores, and neither is locked in for a creditor's horizon. Software recurring revenue was USD 815.8 million at 2026-06-30 and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, about half due within 14 months, which gives visibility. Scores royalties give none because distributors report volumes after the period. Pricing power is evident, since the third-quarter business-to-business increase was attributed to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, but three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of quarterly revenue, they sell a competing score, and the company's own risk factors say fee limits or a regulator's score-choice decision could constrain price. Price, concentration and policy risk are one risk, so revenue is predictable in Software and cyclical, concentrated and exposed to substitution in Scores.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are high and hard to erode through costs but can fall sharply on revenue. Scores segment costs were 10% of segment revenue for nine months, so lost price or volume falls almost entirely to operating income, while Software segment margin fell to 28% from 31% as point-in-time licence sales declined and third-party hosting costs rose. Operating expenses were 47% of revenue, with personnel and hosting the main increases, and 226 positions were removed in fiscal 2025, so cost action is available. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a loss of Scores price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nearly all EBITDA reaches free cash flow before debt repayment: free cash flow was 76.72% of derived EBITDA over twelve months, and capital spending was 1.48% of nine-month revenue. Deferred revenue is customer-funded float rather than payables, and a slowdown in new software bookings could reverse it. Cash interest is the growing leakage, rising from USD 103.56 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 164.87 million over twelve months, and conversion slipped from 78.68% to 76.72% as it rose, with a full year of the new debt still to come.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense in Software and concentrated in Scores. In Software the company names fraud, origination and decisioning competitors such as Nice Actimize, Experian, Pegasystems and SAS and says many competitors are larger. In Scores the one scaled rival is VantageScore, a joint venture of the same three agencies that distribute the FICO Score. Entry is hard because the company holds no consumer credit data of its own and scores are built on agency files, but the housing regulator's validation process lets lenders use other models. Substitutes are in-house models and alternative scores, so price is the lever that most invites substitution, which is an analyst interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high: customers are mostly large banks, insurers and agencies, many larger than the company, that can demand lower prices and non-standard terms, and the three agencies are at once buyers and competitors. Supplier power is moderate: the agencies supply the data behind the scores and distribute them, and third-party cloud and data-centre hosting is a rising cost that management cites for the fall in Software margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit, while social and technology factors are not a primary driver on the supplied materials. Use of the FICO Score for mortgages sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is subject to ongoing validation by those enterprises and their regulator, whose director announced in July 2025 that originators may choose the credit score they submit, and legislative or regulatory limits on score fees could constrain price increases. The company is also subject to consumer-protection supervision and, for products using artificial intelligence, to the European Union's AI Act, which takes effect mostly in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic exposure is direct: banking supplied 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and Scores volumes depend on mortgage and credit card activity, which falls when credit tightens or rates rise. Higher rates also raise the cost of the USD 2,210.00 million of floating-rate debt by about USD 22.10 million a year for each percentage point, so a rate rise that lowers mortgage volume would hit both sides of the cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation CALC-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the 90% Scores margin that supports interest cover, free cash flow that is 76.72% of derived EBITDA, a maturity profile with no large payment before fiscal 2028, and platform software growing recurring revenue while retention is 148%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation CALC-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are derived gross leverage of 4.46x after borrowing-funded repurchases, earnings concentrated in Scores and three distributors, interest that will rise to about USD 316.51 million a year, and a Software segment whose margin fell to 28%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; calculation CALC-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are applying free cash flow to debt, a stated leverage target, and the platform migration raising Software margin and retention.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are a mortgage score price or policy change, the antitrust claim that continues through discovery, floating-rate resets, and a covenant ceiling that steps down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is strong because the FICO Score is the standard measure of consumer credit risk in the United States and revenue was USD 2,393.58 million over twelve months; no peer data is supplied, so the comparison with other leveraged-credit issuers is qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive advantage is strong today and under pressure at the margin: standard-setting use and a 91% third-quarter Scores margin show it, while VantageScore, the regulator's score-choice announcement and in-house models are the routes by which it could erode.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business diversification is weak: Scores produced 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, three agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, financial services supplied 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the Americas 87%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation CALC-04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending of 1.48% of revenue is easy to defer, but the cost base is mostly personnel and hosting, and cutting research and development would slow the platform migration that supports retention.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is average: Scores margin was 88% in each of fiscal 2023 to 2025 and 91% in the third quarter, but Software margin fell from 33% in fiscal 2023 to 30% in fiscal 2025 and 26% in the third quarter, and consolidated margin depends on Scores price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is average: free cash flow rose from USD 607.41 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 960.88 million over twelve months, but conversion slipped and interest at current rates would lower it by about USD 151.64 million a year before tax.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: USD 2.5 billion of notes was placed in ten months and the disclosed fair value was 98.04% of face value, but derived gross leverage of 4.46x is high and no rating or market price is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-03-31_fico-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity position is average: USD 538.44 million of cash and undrawn revolver before letters of credit covers USD 300.00 million of installments, but it is down from USD 859.14 million at the 2025 year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance is weak: cash repurchases were 4.06x free cash flow and were funded by debt, the covenant ceiling reported after the June 2026 amendment is higher than before, and no sponsor or controlling holder is established, although Business & governance rates overall governance risk medium because dividends are absent, no lender-adverse action is recorded and terms are disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Taken together the main supports are cash conversion, margin and a staggered maturity profile, the main constraints are leverage policy and concentration, the trend is weaker on leverage and cover and firmer on free cash flow, and the key missing datapoints are the covenant definition and the price and volume split of Scores growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months management guides fiscal 2026 revenue of USD 2.53 billion, up from USD 2.45 billion in earlier guidance, and the near-term path for creditors is set by whether repurchases slow before the ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31. The first term loan installment of USD 75.00 million is due on 2026-09-30, and installments of USD 300.00 million fall within twelve months. The medium-term outlook of three to five years is not established because no multi-year guidance, rating or market view is supplied.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Company-specific tailwinds are the Scores unit price, platform growth of 62% and net retention of 148%, and free cash flow; headwinds are non-platform runoff of 17%, hosting cost, higher interest cost and the covenant path. Sector tailwinds are not evidenced beyond mortgage and credit card activity, and the sector headwind is regulatory and competitive pressure on score pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with a pricing or policy event in mortgage scores, for example score choice moving volume to a competing score or a distributor winning a lower price. The first operational break is Scores revenue: segment costs are small, so the nine-month increase in Scores segment operating income of USD 363.76 million would reverse almost one for one, taking derived EBITDA from USD 1,252.44 million to USD 888.68 million. Derived gross leverage would reach 6.28x, net leverage 6.00x and, even if share-based compensation of USD 174.29 million were added back, 5.25x, against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x. A reversal of only half the increase gives 5.21x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the second step and holds. After run-rate interest of USD 316.51 million, tax at the nine-month rate and capital spending, about USD 400.83 million of cash would remain against USD 300.00 million of term loan installments, with USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver and repurchases as a lever. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis, but a covenant test on a definition not supplied would be the first constraint, and an amendment of the kind agreed in June 2026 could be needed before the ceiling falls to 4.0x. This is an illustration of mechanics, not a forecast or a default view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Fair Isaac presents a strong business profile supported by a 90% Scores margin and free cash flow of USD 960.88 million, but credit quality is constrained by derived gross leverage of 4.46x built through borrowing-funded repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: conversion is high, but it depends on mortgage score price and three distributors. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on repurchases slowing, on the covenant definition and on continued market access before the fiscal 2028 maturities of USD 1,987.50 million. The primary downside path is a pricing or policy change that reduces Scores earnings while interest and the covenant ceiling tighten. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers the profile is stronger on margin and cash conversion and weaker on leverage, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the price and volume split of Scores growth and market evidence. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: borrowing-funded repurchases against a concentrated earnings base.
